EXACT FILES for this contract (workspace-relative - use these verbatim; do not guess):
  ap-web/src/lib/copy.ts

Create the NEW module ap-web/src/lib/copy.ts. It exports the vocabulary below as named constants (one authoritative mapping object plus direct named exports for the common terms) and a small relativeTime(iso: string): string helper for 'last seen'. No existing file imports it yet - create only this file and modify nothing else.

THE VOCABULARY (authoritative - use these words, do not invent alternatives; import shared strings from '@/lib/copy' rather than re-typing literals):
  warden -> never shown to a user; remove the word entirely
  automaton / automata -> 'saved routine' / 'routines'
  execution -> 'run'
  MCP servers -> 'connected apps'
  ghost dispatch -> 'never started'
  last_heartbeat -> 'last seen' plus a relative time
  context_pct -> 'memory used', shown as a whole percent
  run-weighted / unweighted -> 'across all runs' / 'average per routine'
  fail-closed -> 'stops if a check fails'
  receipt -> 'proof of what was done'
  gate -> 'needs your OK'
  exit code 0 / 3 / 6 -> 'finished' / 'paused for input' / 'failed a check'
  Mtok -> 'per million words'

Change nothing else, in these or any other files, beyond what is described above.

HOW TO WORK:
  - FIRST RESPONSE: propose, in ONE turn, every provenance tool call this contract needs - a read_file for each named file, plus a run_shell find <dir> -maxdepth 1 -name <Stem>*.test.tsx -print for each named file's co-located test - and set done=true on that same turn. Never split discovery across turns: a turn that requests only part of the evidence strands the run, because follow-up revisions cannot execute tool calls.
  - Read every named file with read_file before changing it. Never edit a file you have not successfully read, and never invent its contents.
  - Make each change with a write_file call containing the complete new file contents. Write ONE file per response; when several files are named, take them in successive turns.
  - After the final write, run BOTH gate commands verbatim as run_shell calls:
      npm --prefix ap-web run type-check
      npm --prefix ap-web test
    Run them exactly as written; a scoped variant does not satisfy the gate. Also run git status --porcelain as a run_shell call - it shows new untracked files, which git diff does not - and confirm only the named files (and their co-located tests) changed.
  - Set done=true once the edits are written and both gate commands have run. done is not a claim that the patch is committed - staging and commit are the orchestrator's job.
  - You MAY update a named file's co-located *.test.tsx when your change alters an exported type, prop, or visible string the test asserts. Never delete a test, rename it away, or mark it skip/todo/only; update it to match the new wording.
  - A missing file is a provable fact, not a dead end: prove presence or absence with run_shell find/grep - empty output is positive evidence of absence.
  - If you are challenged and asked to try again, RE-EMIT the complete write_file tool_call. A response containing only {"done": true} is never sufficient: proposals are not carried forward between turns.
  - BASELINE: the suite already skips 1 test file (src/loadtest/streamRenderBench.run.test.ts) and 2 tests. Inherited skips are expected; only an increase above that baseline is a failure.
  - LARGE FILES - SURGICAL EDIT OPTION: when a named file is too large to rewrite faithfully in one response (roughly 25KB or more), do NOT escalate and do NOT attempt the full-file write. Instead perform the change as a three-step sequence: (1) write_file a SHORT one-off script at ap-web/.aos-edit.py that does exact-string replacement on the target (read the target first so match strings are exact; assert each old string occurs exactly once; write the file back); (2) run_shell python3 ap-web/.aos-edit.py — note inline python3 -c is not permitted by the sandbox, but running a script file is; (3) run_shell rm ap-web/.aos-edit.py so the helper never appears in scope checks. Then run git diff -- <file> as a run_shell call and inspect that the diff is precisely the intended change. A verified surgical edit fully satisfies a write requirement.
  - Change nothing else.
